leakage_signals: No private history is provided, but the options expose preference-sensitive attributes: window versus aisle seating, tolerance for short connections, willingness to make an extra connection, arrival-time priorities, and whether reimbursed fare differences should still influence the recommendation.
verdict.rationale: All options meet the only explicit timing constraint. B is fastest and has one connection, but its 55-minute ATL connection is materially tighter than the alternatives. A trades a much later arrival for a long, lower-risk connection and a lower listed fare. C is the least expensive and has longer connection buffers, but adds a second connection and arrives later than B or D. D arrives relatively early and has a more forgiving connection than B, but costs more and offers an aisle rather than a window. Choosing among speed, connection-risk tolerance, itinerary simplicity, fare stewardship, and window-versus-aisle seating requires unstated preferences.
